newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs, fuel gain but others hold.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs, fuel gain but others hold.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to firmer on Thursday with Brent CFDs leading the gains.
Dealers said CFDs rose by several cents while heavy fuel gained $1. Gasoline and naphtha swaps were unchanged and slow.

Brent CFDs gained up to 13 cents with July 21-25 pegged around flat to +1.0 cent against September Brent from -12/13 cents while July 28 - August 8 rose to -8/9 cents from -15 cents. August 4-8 firmed to -13 cents against September from -19 cents and August 11-15 went to -14 cents from -20 cents.
A July 21-25 CFD was sold at -2 cents against September.

Dealers said the strength in CFDs was on the back of a stronger wet deal on Wednesday and talk of a trader/refiner seeking a ULCC load to take transatlantic. Some traders said the market was under some manipulation for higher numbers.
Heavy fuel bounced up $1.0 or so with July trading at $87.50 and August at $88.50. Physical barges were done at $88.50 for Antwerp and Rotterdam.

Gasoline swaps were steady, consolidating after recent gains. August was pegged around $189.50 with September backwardated by $2 or so. Strong U.S. prices backed by good demand was likely to underpin the European prices given the arbitrage potential.
Naphtha was also in a consolidating phase with August talked around $188.00 and September around $186.00. Nothing was heard done, but the levels broadly matched physical numbers.
